summary.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q2 FY27 revenue hit record INR235 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR15.1 crore, but management flagged weak FIBC volumes and European demand.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR235 crore was the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with PAT of INR15.1 crore, more than double year-on-year. Manufacturing segment margin rose to 11.65% from 8.95% in Q1 on price pass-through, while manufacturing volumes fell (exports 4,757 tons vs 6,591 tons). About INR12.4 crore of DFIA export incentive, which was suspended in Q1 FY27, inflated the quarter and is treated as partly non-recurring. Management expects volumes to stay soft in the near term, citing European destocking, high polymer prices, freight and El Nino effects.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Segment margin 11.65% vs 8.95% in Q1 FY27 and 6.34% in Q2 FY26. Average selling price up 14% QoQ; export sales INR119.81 crore on 4,757 tons vs INR119.16 crore on 6,591 tons a year earlier.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore vs INR16.87 crore in Q2 FY26; trading profit INR1.16 crore vs INR0.59 crore.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: FIBC rose to 66% of manufacturing revenue from 54%; fabrics fell to 18% from 20%; multifilament 9% from 8%; UV masterbatches, small bags and geo fabrics each under 3%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe 65% of mix, North America 17%, South America 14%, balance Australia, Asia and Africa.

segments.name: Valex Ventures (UK subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Returned to profit in Q2 FY27 after a small loss in Q1, helped by customer supplies after the UK FTA and restructuring.

segments.name: ESSEKAN JV (Taslan yarn)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR38 lakh vs INR22 lakh in Q1; FY28 target INR10-12 crore; utilisation still very low.

guidance_outlook: FIBC manufacturing volume expected up only 5-10% in FY27; about 20% growth targeted in FY28. Revenue growth in FY27 expected from higher prices.
Non-woven revenue expected at INR100-120 crore in FY27-28 (as answered on the call); management pointed to a 14-15% margin expectation, which it said is the expectation.
Export incentive (DFIA) expected to run at INR3-4 crore per quarter going forward; DFIA was suspended in Q1 FY27.
Management declined to give H2 EBITDA margin guidance, citing volatility and non-woven trial and approval timelines.
Peak debt expected at about INR40-45 crore by end FY27 on the new project term loan.
capex_capacity: FIBC capacity to rise to about 24,000 tons per annum from about 18,000 tons, adding about 6,000 tons in phases over five years; ground floor of Unit 3 operational, first and second floors due by end-November 2026.

Non-woven facility: capacity about 12,000 tons per year; first line (needle punching) to commission by 15 November 2026, second machine by mid-February 2027. Half of capacity arrives this quarter, half by end of next quarter.
Multifilament yarn capacity about 10,000 tons per year, up from about 7,000 tons. Geotextile capacity about 2,500-3,000 tons.
Project cost INR106.9 crore; INR78.86 crore incurred (about 74%) as of 20 October 2026. Delays from monsoon rain and overseas machine commissioning/visa issues.
Capital WIP rose about INR37 crore in H1 to INR45.67 crore; YES Bank term loan INR40 crore sanctioned, INR27.38 crore availed as of 30 September.
demand_pricing: Customers are destocking after high polymer prices; management estimated about 40% of destocking capacity used in Q1 and a further 30% expected in Q2 FY27.
Manufacturing volumes fell year-on-year; average order quantity dipped; most orders dispatch within a month, with 3-4 weeks of demand visibility.
Polymer (PP) prices rebounded to near March 2026 highs by September after a July dip; ocean freight high and Kanpur ICD container availability affected landed costs.
Management says it is protecting realisations; Europe slowdown is the main concern, with high energy costs in Germany hitting the chemical sector.
Receivables rose INR26.32 crore to INR120.6 crore in line with higher selling prices; management said receivables were kept in line.
Record number of customer visits during the quarter; company exploring inorganic opportunities in India and overseas, with nothing material identified yet.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how the company managed raw material volatility across the quarter and what the capacity increase looks like over two years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polymer prices dipped in July on surplus then recovered by September. Non-woven capacity is about 12,000 tons per year, FIBC will rise to 24,000 tons, and yarn capacity is 10,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how much channel destocking has happened and how much could follow.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated destocking capability at 100 units, with about 40 done in Q1 and about 30 more expected in Q2. Management said manufacturing volume has gone down and that it cannot forecast the war or energy crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about peak debt and debt-to-equity for FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said peak debt would be about INR40-45 crore by end FY27 on the new INR40 crore term loan, with INR27 crore already drawn. Short-term borrowing is driven by raw material prices. Debt-to-equity was 0.56x at 30 September, with net worth of INR290.56 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the top-line contribution from the non-woven business and FIBC volumes in FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: Non-woven revenue expected at INR100-120 crore in FY27-28. FIBC manufacturing volume up only 5-10% in FY27 and about 20% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how much of other operating income is recurring.
qa_highlights.answer: Other operating income was INR13.11 crore, including INR12.4 crore DFIA and INR0.34 crore IOCL. Management expects INR3-4 crore per quarter of export incentives to recur. Analyst estimated about INR6 crore of Q1+Q2 DFIA as non-recurring, which management agreed with.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for H2 EBITDA margin expectations and how the expanded FIBC capacity will be sold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a margin range and said volumes depend on demand revival, not on capacity. It is expanding into new geographies.

risks_watch: Europe demand weakness (about 65% of revenue) and customer destocking; management says volumes may stay affected for one to two quarters.
Non-woven commissioning slippage (first line targeted 15 November 2026; second in mid-February 2027) and the 14-15% margin target not yet proven.
Debt rising: borrowings INR162.61 crore at 30 September (from INR132 crore at 30 June); short-term debt sensitive to polymer prices.
Other income includes a INR5.57 crore H1 forex gain, and DFIA incentives were suspended in Q1, so reported profit may normalise.
Management declined to quantify H2 margins, so near-term earnings visibility is limited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the financial result and the customer base but cautious on near-term demand. Management repeatedly said volumes will stay soft and avoided H2 margin or volume guidance, and some answers on capacity and debt were unclear.
key_quotes: Revenue for the quarter stood at INR235 crores, the highest quarterly revenue in the company's history and profit after tax more than doubled year-on-year to INR 15.1 crores.

Rather than pursuing growth purely through higher volumes, we remain committed to improving our product portfolio, expanding into value-added applications and building capabilities that support sustainable profitability over the long term.
We are seeing a slowdown from our customers in Europe.
We would not like to give specific numbers at this stage.

growth.why: FIBC volume guidance cut to only +5-10% in FY27 amid weak European demand, with FY27 revenue growth expected from price; non-woven (INR100-120 cr FY27-28) and FIBC capacity additions are under construction with timelines in Nov 2026 to Feb 2027 but project is ~74% spent and delayed by monsoon and machine commissioning issues.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Manufacturing segment margin rose to 11.65% from 8.95% in Q1 on price pass-through, but consolidated EBITDA margin slipped to 9.83% from 10.67% a year ago, H2 margin guidance was declined, and about INR6 crore of DFIA is non-recurring.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Non-woven first line (needle punching) due 15 Nov 2026 and second machine by mid-Feb 2027 (~12,000 tpa, INR106.9 crore project ~74% spent); FIBC Unit 3 first and second floors due by end-Nov 2026 (capacity ~18,000 to ~24,000 tpa).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FIBC manufacturing volume guided only +5-10% for FY27 and manufacturing volume fell YoY (exports 4,757 tons vs 6,591 tons), with about 40% of destocking done in Q1 and a further 30% expected in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, but the company is already spending INR106.9 crore on non-woven plus FIBC expansion, and management says volumes depend on demand revival rather than capacity, which limits the case for a fresh project in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FIBC volume only +5-10% for FY27 and declined to give H2 EBITDA margin guidance, citing volatility and non-woven approval timelines.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Europe is about 65% of revenue with destocking ongoing, DFIA of INR3-4 crore per quarter replaces the INR12.4 crore one-off, and non-woven commissioning could slip further after monsoon and machine delays.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Non-woven fabric is the new product line, due to commission 15 Nov 2026 and mid-Feb 2027, targeting INR100-120 crore revenue over FY27-28; multifilament yarn capacity rises from ~7,000 to ~10,000 tpa.

rows.label: Price pass-through lifting realisations
rows.why: Average selling price rose 14% QoQ and management says FY27 revenue growth will come from higher prices rather than volumes, though polymer prices rebounded to near March 2026 highs in September.

rows.label: Peak debt rising to INR40-45 crore
rows.why: Borrowings rose to INR162.61 crore at 30 September from INR132 crore at 30 June, with peak debt guided at INR40-45 crore by end FY27 on the new term loan (INR27.38 crore drawn of INR40 crore sanctioned).

rows.label: Receivables rising with prices
rows.why: Receivables rose INR26.32 crore to INR120.6 crore in line with higher selling prices, which ties up working capital while volumes are soft.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record result and customer base but cautious on near-term volumes, and declined H2 margin and volume guidance; analysts pressed on recurring income (DFIA), debt, and the non-woven and FIBC capacity timelines.
